content: This medication is used to treat a variety of serious and potentially life-threatening fungal infections. It is typically administered via injection into a vein as directed by your doctor, usually once a day or every other day. The injection should be given slowly over a period of 2 to 6 hours. Your doctor may start with a smaller test dose to evaluate your response to the medication. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, body weight, response to the test dose, and overall response to treatment. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use it. Before use, visually inspect the product for any particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Infusion reactions may occur during the administration of this drug. To minimize these side effects, your doctor may prescribe additional medications, such as acetaminophen, diphenhydramine, or corticosteroids like hydrocortisone, before each treatment. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of infusion reactions, such as fever, shaking, chills, flushing, loss of appetite, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, headache, shortness of breath, or rapid breathing. Treatment with this medication may need to continue for several weeks to several months, depending on the type of infection being treated. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, if you experience any signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney and liver function, potassium and magnesium levels, and complete blood counts) should be performed regularly while you are using this medication. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Proper storage of this medication is essential. Consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
